correctness.rationale: The graph product distance is Manhattan distance, making all and only nonempty convex sets coordinate rectangles. The extremum exclusion criterion is necessary and sufficient for all traces. Unique obstructing points and weak-quadrant inclusion–exclusion give the cubic coefficient; a unique left/right/bottom/top bijection and exact squared-gap sums give the quartic coefficient. Boundary cases m,n=1 or 2 and limits are handled. Finite independent checks ran successfully, but are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: Instead of only the textbook maximum shatterable support size, the result evaluates every degree of the shattering polynomial for all finite two-dimensional path grids. It distinguishes slender and full grids, accounts exactly for tied coordinates, and yields two meaningful random-support limiting probabilities (2/3, 1/6). The cubic correction and quartic factorization have independent combinatorial explanations; this is not just a renamed VC-four bound.
